title: README
universal_lens: The Higgsfield architecture defines a categorical fibration where the canonical SDK acts as the base category of stateful observables, while React bindings and Quanta design tokens form fiber categories. The CLI synchronization enforces a strict pullback diagram, ensuring local workspace snapshots remain isomorphic to the global source-of-truth under continuous structural deformation.

The `sync` operation functions as a Bayesian update, projecting high-dimensional telemetry into a conformal prediction set. The ignored template snapshot acts as a localized posterior approximation, continuously calibrated against the global truth to minimize epistemic variance in sports intelligence inference.
gse_mapping: For GSE, the repository root models the global game-state manifold. Scaffolding a new app corresponds to initializing a situational reasoning context. The `@higgsfield/fnf-react` controllers act as Hamiltonian flow operators, dictating valid state-transitions between tactical formations, while the landing blocks enforce boundary conditions on the generated playbooks.

The 'Canonical Higgsfield packages' serve as the base space $B$, containing the fundamental algebraic structures (SDK core, jobs, media). Each generated application template represents a point $x \in B$, with its local `app/packages` snapshot acting as the fiber $F_x$. The strict instruction to 'never patch a generated template's ignored snapshot directly' establishes a vertical transport constraint; modifications must occur strictly within the base space. The `node cli/src/index.js sync` command functions as the horizontal lift, propagating changes from the base space down to the fibers, ensuring the entire bundle remains trivialized and structurally coherent. In this framework, `@higgsfield/fnf` provides the connection form, defining how state flows between modules, while `@higgsfield/quanta` dictates the metric tensor, enforcing visual and dimensional consistency across all fibers. The breakdown regime emerges if the horizontal lift fails—i.e., if the sync process cannot resolve conflicting updates, leading to torsion in the workspace graph. reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This architectural pattern descends from the Unix philosophy of separation of concerns, evolving through the modular monolith designs of the early 2000s. It heavily borrows from category theory, specifically the concept of adjoint functors used in modern dependency injection frameworks. The explicit prohibition against direct patching echoes the immutability principles introduced by functional programming languages like Haskell, ensuring referential transparency across the software lifecycle.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model two primary agents: the Core Architect and the Template Developer. The Core Architect operates at the base space level, optimizing for global consistency and API stability. They assume the Template Developer will inevitably attempt shortcuts. Conversely, the Template Developer seeks rapid iteration and assumes the sync mechanism is infallible. The `AGENTS.md` files act as a shared mental model, aligning these opposing incentives by explicitly documenting the boundaries of agency and the consequences of violating the fibration constraints.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A veto condition is triggered if a change in the `@higgsfield/fnf` core introduces a breaking API change that the `fnf-react` binding cannot transparently adapt to. This represents a leakage of complexity from the base layer into the fiber layer. To maintain anti-collinearity, any modification to the SDK core must be accompanied by a corresponding update to the React provider's type definitions before the `sync` command is permitted to execute, preventing the propagation of ill-typed states into the user-facing applications.
